text:
Maya: CI failure on PR #9287 microbench: noticed a ~12% drop in batches/sec for short sequences after the merge. Failing on ubuntu-gpu-rt-3.2 job. Logs attached below. :eyes:

Ethan: which test exactly? microbench name?

Maya: `microbench/throughput/small_seq_batches`
CI output snippet:
```
FAIL: small_seq_batches: baseline=4800 iters/sec, current=4210 iters/sec (delta -12.3%, threshold -10.0%)
Trace: runtime/batcher: timer drift -> more empty waits?
Cmd: pytest tests/microbench/test_small_seq.py::test_batches_per_sec -k small_seq --bench
```

CI-Bot: [job link] ubuntu-gpu-rt-3.2 — FAILED (bench delta) :warning:

Arjun: hm, recent merge I suspect is 9214 which tweaked the batch timer rounding & the wake path. @Lin did that touch the scheduler?

Lin: yep 9214 changed batch_timer.round_up_ms from 2 -> 1 to reduce latency for tiny requests. The intent was better tail, but I didn't stress the small-seq throughput microbench.

Sofia: could be more frequent wakeups causing higher sync overhead on the KV cache hotpath. We saw similar overhead when timer granularity changed in a libuv patch before. Can you dump perf counters or a short pprof?

Maya: ran a quick perf on a repro GPU worker, here's the callhot (top 6):
```
%  samples  symbol
21.4  6420    runtime::batcher::wait_loop
18.3  5480    cuda_kv_store::touch_entry
12.1  3620    scheduler::wakeup_delayed
9.8   2930    memory::alloc_small
6.5   1950    kernel_selector::select
4.7   1410    other
```
There's a spike in wait_loop/syscalls that correlates with more frequent timer wakeups.

Ethan: interesting that kernel_selector is showing too. Could be the timer change increases contention and changes the kernel choice distribution for short batches. That could worsen throughput for those microbenches.

Arjun: I'll run a quick bisect across merges since 9210..9220 to confirm. If 9214 is the culprit we should either revert or gate the change behind the opt-in flag for now (don't want to block the entire release).

Lin: I can push a toggled revert (flip to previous rounding) as a hotfix candidate. Also will add a microbench in the PR checks to catch this pattern.

Sofia: please add a golden for small_seq_batches with CI threshold tightened to avoid flakiness. Also log kernel_selection stats in the bench output so we can see distribution changes.

Maya: for immediate rollout blocker? I'd prefer gating the change on dedicated GPU pools only, or revert until we add the bench and instrumentation. We have customers who depend on small-seq QPS.

Arjun: agreed. Opening a PR to revert 9214 -> 9214-revert (draft) and starting a CI run locally now. If local reproduces, we'll push draft revert and run full CI.

CI-Bot: Started job: eng-runtime/PR-#9290-revert-9214 — running microbench suite.

Ethan: once reverted, let's also add a unit-style test that asserts kernel_selector distribution doesn't shift >5% for small sequences when timer granularity changes. That should catch regression without blocking feature work.

Maya: thanks everyone. Please post results in this thread. If revert fixes it, we'll ship a follow-up with better instrumentation and a canary rollout. :thumbsup:

Arjun: local CI green for microbench after revert. pushing draft now.

Lin: noted — I'll follow up with the opt-in flag PR and the added microbench.

CI-Bot: Job finished: eng-runtime/PR-#9290-revert-9214 — PASSED microbench suite :white_check_mark:

Maya: great — marking this thread as a temporary rollout blocker until revert merges to main. Will re-run full canary after merge.

Sofia: opened issue RN-2047 to track instrumentation + golden test.

Maya: closing loop once canary validates. Thanks all :heart:
